If the shear viscosity is non-zero, the dispersion equation for shear modes becomes increasingly complex, whereas the fluid's viscosity has minimal impact on acoustic modes, except when the fluid's speed of sound approaches one. If the shear viscosity is instead assumed to be zero, both shear and acoustic modes exhibit minimal compression, resulting in significantly lower group velocities compared to the zero-viscosity case. We have verified that even when the fluid's speed of sound approaches one, certain conditions apply - specifically that the group velocity is lower than the speed of light - for both shear and acoustic modes. Furthermore, we found that when the fluid's speed of sound is greater than one, both shear and acoustic modes have lower group velocities.

Our research explores the potential for primordial black holes (PBHs) to serve as a source of the cosmic microwave background's (CMB's) anisotropies, leveraging the constraints imposed by the CMB's itself. To determine the mass and fractional abundance of PBHs, we consider three distinct formation mechanisms, namely collapse during the radiation-dominated era, initially stable PBHs forming in protogalactic clouds, and PBHs created through oscillations between an overdense and an underdense state. Assuming that the PBHs' initial mass is in the range of $10^{-16}$ to $10^{-13}$ gramms, the anisotropies they produce would be consistent with CMB observations. This prediction, however, conflicts with direct searches for PBHs, unless the PBHs' initial mass is at the higher end of this range. In that case, the discrepancy could be explained if PBHs lost a significant portion of their mass due to, for example, interactions with dark matter.

Introducing the Virtual Protected Framework, a cutting-edge approach that seamlessly integrates a multi-layered hardware neural network, specifically designed for Vanilla Multi-Layer Perceptron neural network implementations, directly onto Intel's N3000-based UltraSPARC+ T2 chips via a Trusted Execution Environment. This approach leverages the Transient Fault Hardware Environment to create a secure and reliable environment for neural network computations on untrusted host systems. The Virtual Protected Framework operates within this Trusted Execution Environment, comprised of five distinct stages: Program Setup, Data Setup, Activation, Weight Multiplication, and Output Production. Each stage is designed to take advantage of Intel's Integrated R5 Coprocessor, as well as the SPARC architecture's built-in security features, all within a five-stage pipeline structure. This architecture offers enhanced performance, as well as a notable decrease in overhead, thanks to its hybrid approach that combines Fixed Point Arithmetic and Binary Arithmetic on the Coprocessor, as part of the arithmetic logic unit. Additionally, this approach provides a notable increase in energy efficiency via dynamic and static power savings. Furthermore, this design offers protection against malicious attacks on the Input/Output modules, as well as against side-channel attacks that target the main processor, thanks to its ability to isolate and contain threats within the Trusted Execution Environment.

Researchers investigate polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTAS) for solving specific constraint satisfaction problems, such as Maximum Independent Set or Graph Coloring. A particular class of problems includes those with general weighted CSPs. Developing a PTAS for such problems is even more challenging than finding one for their unweighted counterparts with NP-hard approximation. Our research focuses on finding a PTAS for the maximum general-weighted CSP with constraints based on linear clauses. This involves solving a specific geometric problem in higher dimensions, for which we propose a solution that works for dimensions $d \leq n-1$ and certain computational resources. This PTAS has a resource-efficient version that applies to $d \leq n/2$ and certain other resources. This approximation scheme can be applied to CSPs with additional properties, including sparsity and extreme properties. It's also useful for convex geometrical constraints, although it doesn't work for all linear constraints. Our approach combines several techniques, including a PTAS for the geometric problem, a linear programming relaxation with restricted constraints, and obtaining a sparse solution from a combination of this relaxation and the Epsilon-N scheme. This PTAS has a threshold-based version that applies to CSPs with extreme properties. Our research also provides a PTAS for finding all solutions to CSPs with constraints based on linear clauses, provided a certain approximation threshold is met. Our approach to solving the geometric problem depends on testing linear spaces, which we prove to be complete for a specific class of problems with random or

Pretrained language models, renowned for their versatility, have been shown to be effective in a range of tasks including unsupervised and few-shot learning. This paper delves into the potential of these models by examining their performance in three areas: (1) uncovering semantic relationships from raw text without labels; (2) achieving high accuracy in tasks with limited labeled data; and (3) achieving accuracy superior to shallow methods in semantic parsing. The experiments reveal that these models can accomplished the aforementioned tasks with considerable success. Notably, their success in few-shot learning stems from their ability to leverage the substantial unlabeled data at their disposal, whereas their strong performance in unsupervised and shallow semantic parsing tasks can be attributed to characteristics of the data itself. The code and the fine-tuned models used in the study have been made available online.

The integration of hyperspectral images (HSI) and computer vision in urban hyperspectral segmentation is a developing field. HSI, which capture more detail than traditional RGB images, require sophisticated analysis. This study harnesses the enhanced informational capabilities of HSI to tackle the complex task of urban hyperspectral segmentation. Building on existing research into HSI analysis and driven by the potential offered by this technology, we investigate its application in semantic segmentation. This study is particularly geared towards utilizing the features of HSI for analyzing segmented images, a practice also known as weakly-guided segmentation. We develop an innovative framework that leverages a two-stage approach, combining an HSI-based hyperspectral image generation step with a traditional semantic segmentation process. The integration of this HSI information into standard semantic segmentation techniques demonstrates the significant potential offered by HSI, which enables the creation of high-quality hyperspectral images even in situations of limited availability of labeled data. This success is attributed to the unique ability of HSI to distinguish between fine details, which typically pose significant challenges to computer vision applications. The potential offered by HSI has now made urban hyperspectral segmentation more accessible.

The unique rotational characteristics of (10199) Halwey, an ultra-red and extremely fast-spinning early member of the main sequence, present an intriguing phenomenon that demands explanation. We contend that one of the least understood processes in planetary science, planetary ingestion by a multiple star system, could be the primary driver of this asteroid's rapid rotation. However, the transfer of angular momentum from the planet-asteroid system to the stars requires further investigation. To resolve the uncertainty surrounding angular momentum transfer, we carried out a thorough analysis of the system's 2D and 3D structure, employing numerical simulations that incorporated the asteroid's initial orbital conditions and the stars' current properties. Our findings show that the asteroid likely originated from the planet-asteroid system, given that the stars' current configuration matches the predictions of the planetary ingestion model. Additionally, our research reveals that the loss of the asteroid's initial binary companion, likely within the first million years of the system's evolution, could be the key to understanding the asteroid's current rapid rotation. Finally, we make recommendations for future follow-up studies, including a thorough examination of the system's spectral characteristics, which could help verify our theoretical predictions of the planetary ingestion model.

We examine the interconnection between the fast multiplication of natural numbers in the RAM model with addition and other rapid operations like exponentiation, root extraction, and logarithmic functions. We demonstrate that if we can multiply two $n$-bit numbers in $O(n^c)$ time for some $c < 2$, then we can perform several other operations such as calculating the $m$-th power of a number, finding the $m$-th root of a number, and determining whether a number is a perfect power, all within the same time complexity. We further investigate how these results are related to established lower bounds for multiplication. We show that if we can efficiently compute logarithms and roots, then we can establish a constant better than $\frac{2}{n}$ addition lower bound for multiplying $n$-bit numbers, building on existing research.

To assist users in finding the best items from extensive product collections, session-based suggestion aims to provide personalized recommendations at the individual user session level. The standard framework for making such suggestions relies on user-interest driven item ranking. However, since user sessions encompass varied durations and item collections comprise numerous products, ensuring that suggestions are both relevant and comprehensive can be challenging. Especially in cases where data is scarce, enhancing suggestion quality is crucial. In order to address these challenges, this research introduces an innovative approach called Self-Guided Graph Co-Training, which combines user-generated and system-generated hints to enhance suggestion quality. The proposed method capitalizes on the strengths of both human and automated cues, leveraging them to improve the coverage and accuracy of session-based suggestions. Evaluations of SGGT demonstrate superior performance compared to existing methods in terms of both density and diversity of suggested items.

This research presents a novel method for generating LCD codes using group rings. We extend the concepts of LCD codes, primarily defined using the Radaoui's approach, to the context of group rings. Within this framework, we introduce two types of group LCD codes - group LCD and group invertible LCD codes. A general approach to constructing the former is provided, along with a specific example. The latter, which is a subset of group LCD codes, is shown to be an LCD code when a certain condition is met, and we present an example as well.

This research examines various differential systems appearing in the study of Calabi-Yau manifolds, particularly those arising from the geometry of metric graphs. Our findings reveal that the differential maps exhibiting an algebraic relationship are indeed constant, leading to the emergence of a global solution. Furthermore, we establish a relationship between these algebraic differential maps and the Feynman integrals of quantum field theory, demonstrating that they represent a specific type of global solution. Notably, the study of Feynman integrals involves analogous differential systems, but with flat connections.

In various object categorization tasks, particularly in visually complex conditions, the deployment of higher-level object attributes such as shape, form, and parts, as well as lower-level visual features, becomes essential for accurate identification. The role of object attributes in visual processing is well documented, but the mechanisms by which they interact with lower-level visual features, specifically in the context of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) used in object classification, remains poorly understood.

Our investigation demonstrates that trained object classifiers comprising simple convolutional neural networks (CNNs) followed by RNNs utilize visual object attributes to perform categorization tasks. The findings indicate that the extraction of object attributes is a critical function of the RNN component, and that visual features within the CNN facilitate the separation of distinct object categories primarily through the integration of attribute information processed by the RNN.

Notably, the effectiveness of attributes in driving information processing within the RNN is heightened when they define unique and distinct categories, and occurs naturally within object categories characterized by varying shapes, forms, and parts, such as those used in our studies involving furniture and nonlinear objects. These conclusions are supported by both human and model object classification performances, and the interplay between visual object attributes and lower-level visual features, specifically in the context of RNN-trained object classifiers, is quantitatively mapped.

Despite the numerous types of one-dimensional non-Hermitian topological structures that have been established, there is no clear classification system for them yet. We show that a specific point-gap topology in one-dimensional systems with non-Hermitian characteristics can be reduced by introducing interactions among fermions. By using a non-Hermitian generalization of the Hubbard model, we find that interactions cause a non-Hermitian topological edge mode to transition into a localized state within one of the system's boundaries. The mode is found to exhibit a semiparametric separation into two distinct types of fermionic elementary particles, which is a novel development in the field of non-Hermitian topology. Additionally, we explore the relationship between the non-Hermitian flux through the system, which is controlled by the hopping amplitude in the transverse direction, and the correlation-driven reduction of the point-gap topology. We also document the regulated reduction of the point-gap topology in systems that contain multiple bands. Finally, we propose that the stabilized correlations in the system could be used to manufacture devices such as bosonic solitons and turn off their transport abilities.

A unimodular matrix that generates a Golay complementary matrix of size $2m \times 2nm$ when augmented by a $2m \times 2m$ identity matrix has been identified for all odd numbers of rows in Golay complementary sets of size $2m$. Specifically, we have developed four phase Golay complementary sets of size $16 \times 8$ and four polyphase sets of size $18 \times 9$. Furthermore, we propose a method to create a set of size $2m \times 2nm + 2 \times 2m$ and show that the feasibility of $m mod 4 = 1$ or $m mod 4 = 3$ depends on the existence of Golay complementary sets of size $2m$. We present four nonrectangular Golay complementary sets of size $16 \times 8$ with four distinct Golay complementary sets of size $18 \times 9$.

We examine predictions from three theoretical models - the Standard Model (SM) with narrow width assumptions, and two alternative theories with broad widths. In this investigation, we analyze the Higgs boson production in proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV, focusing on the four-lepton final state. It is observed that off-shell Higgs measurements are particularly sensitive to the particle's width, whereas on-shell rates are less affected. The analysis suggests that with 300000 events for the four-lepton, 120 GeV Higgs channel, width constraints can be limited to approximately ±25%. Additionally, the study reveals that if the Higgs width is contained within the experimental uncertainty (±25%), then the individual coupling ratios of the Higgs interactions with the W and Z bosons are constrained to be within a 10% margin of the SM predictions.

Biological processes such as plant leaf alterations can be thoroughly analyzed by high-resolution hyperspectral images, revealing inherent characteristics of alterations, but standard classification methods are unable to account for data variability. To address this, we introduce an unsupervised detection method utilizing a novel combination of features for alteration identification that leverages spatial and spectral correlations within hyperspectral images. To effectively learn compact and preservation-friendly representations for alteration detection, we introduce three distinct datasets with altered pixels, utilizing synthetic and real-world hyperspectral images. Furthermore, we propose a novel cost function that optimizes reconstruction error and clustering results, and refine a deep convolutional autoencoder to accommodate cluster labels. Experimental outcomes demonstrate the efficacy of our method in detecting alterations while handling variable hyperspectral images.

A property of squares within the additive group of integers has been explored, specifically regarding the existence of a single addition operation that yields another square when performed on a given square. Certain conditions that ensure the existence of such additive operations have been established, along with an investigation of their infinite counterparts. These conditions can be interpreted as providing two distinct arithmetic interpretations of the third syndrome of the Gauss curve, which arises in the study of the curve's solubility property.

Quantum bits constructed with silicon vacancies hold great promise for the reliable creation of complex optical-photon devices. However, the precise functioning of these quantum bits is compromised by the presence of silicon impurities, which introduce extra valley states. Researchers have developed a technique for measuring the interaction between these valley states and have successfully detected the interaction between adjacent silicon divacancies at atomic scale distances. The measurement reveals that, at close range, the interaction is governed by exchange forces but, at longer distances, it is controlled by longer-range weaker forces. The discovery of these different interactions could lead to the development of new methods for measuring the distance between quantum bits and for the precise control of delocalized states.

Several disciplines such as computer design, operations research, artificial intelligence, and engineering make use of optimization techniques to solve problems. Despite its vital role, implementing optimization solutions often remains a difficult task due to the various requirements and complexities involved. A comprehensive framework, such as CUDA and OpenCL, addresses this challenge by providing a high-level platform for developers to leverage existing code and streamline the development process. However, when we evaluated these options against a specific problem in our recent study, we found them to be deficient in certain key areas. In response, we present LibOPT, an open-source framework designed to rapidly prototype and demonstrate optimization techniques efficiently. By integrating techniques from the field of soft computing, such as fuzzy logic and neural computing, into our framework, we show that LibOPT's implementation is significantly faster and more efficient than its competitors.

Given a field extension K/K0 and a finite transitive group G, we investigate uniform varieties of a specific type and establish a bound for the transference degree in relation to [K : K0] and |G| in general, as well as under additional conditions such as being absolutely irreducible. This result has implications in Weil's criterion for irreducibility and generalizes existing formulas for specific types of varieties.

For decades, the principles of quantum theory and special relativity have been seamlessly integrated into quantum field theory, a widely accepted framework that has also accurately predicted numerous particle physics results. However, discussions surrounding the application of quantum theory to macroscopic spacetime have led to the development of non-commutative geometry, a mathematical framework where spatial coordinates become operators in an underlying Hilbert space. Despite the potential of non-commutative geometry to resolve singularities and the associated problems in black holes and particle physics, its general acceptance in the theoretical physics community remains lacking. A key area of contention lies in the fact that the geometric properties implied by non-commutative geometry appear to contradict both special relativity and the basic tenets of quantum theory, concerns that we will detail and then conclude with a summary of the outstanding challenges still faced by the community.

We introduce an innovative technique for examining the three-dimensional charge transport properties in wide bandgap materials. This approach combines a synthetic single-crystalline diamond sample and a custom-designed charge amplifier system. In our experiments, a femtosecond laser is utilized for two-photon absorption, and we record the resulting transient currents generated within the sample. By rotating the sample and collecting data at various angles, we acquire a three-dimensional map of its charge transport characteristics. We discovered that the charge transport coefficient linearly decreases with increasing charge density, and our findings align well with theoretical predictions. This technique offers the capability to investigate three-dimensional charge transport properties in materials under minimal to no surface modification, utilizing a charge amplifier system with a low noise floor of 5 nA and a response time of 50 ps.

Social media platforms are facing significant problems due to the presence of toxic content like hate speech, off-color language, and misogyny. These difficulties are compounded by the lack of comprehensive and efficient content filtering systems. In this context, our research focuses on addressing the issue of misogyny in Arabic social media posts, which are particularly challenging to process due to limited resources for Arabic NLP tasks. We propose an innovative approach to detect and categorize misogynous content, which is a novel area of study. Our contributions include the identification of relevant features, the design of a deep multi-task learning framework, and an analysis of pre-trained models as potential solutions. We also make our data available for future research by releasing an annotated dataset of misogynous Arabic social media posts. Extensive experimental results show that our proposed approach achieves superior performance compared to existing baseline methods.

This study centres around the solvability of a distinct class of fractional backward stochastic differential equations, which are defined in a probabilistic space, and based on an assumption of Lipschitz continuity in the state variable and delayed existence for the partial differential operator. The proof of existence relies on the approach of a Monte Carlo method combined with the time discretization and stochastic inversion algorithm.

For safety-critical systems, developers of automated systems are under pressure to prove that their controllers can withstand all possible failures and remain safe. Although some methods have been able to demonstrate this level of robustness, they typically require extensive system knowledge and can be very expensive to verify. We have developed a new search algorithm that combines model-based and search approaches to find robust controllers with a more manageable verification cost. By representing the system as a probabilistic model and searching for optimal policies, the need for extensive system knowledge is eliminated. We have successfully applied this method to a range of critical systems, such as traffic lights, air traffic control, and self-healing power systems, ultimately achieving substantial cost savings.

A shared communication link can be the bottleneck in various tasks such as computation and caching. Techniques like encoding and arbitration help mitigate this issue, but the multiple methods and frameworks for analyzing such problems often create confusion. We are introducing a unifying approach that simplifies the study and comparison of different caching and computation strategies. Our framework allows us to examine a wide range of caching methods, including those that utilize side information and time-dependent decoding, as well as demand-based arbitration. We are demonstrating that various existing methods can be encompassed within our framework and providing a method to evaluate their performance under different parameter settings. Furthermore, our framework enables the exploration of novel caching policies and simulation results are presented to illustrate its potential.

We establish a relationship between the univalent reformulation of the Paulin-Mechtey-Ghani framework and the Scott framework by demonstrating that the Scott framework's underlying type theory is equivalent to the univalent extension of the $\lambda_\omega$ calculus. In the process, we also reinterpret the concepts of weak and strong monadicity within the context of univalent type theory, and our findings apply to any type theory that includes a meaningful separation between types of functions and those that act monadically. Notably, although the univalent reformulation of the Scott framework retains the core definitions from its preface, the proof that the monad is strong is simplified when embedded within univalent type theory.

This study expands upon Aoki and Ramaré's findings, specifically their Theorem 1, by removing the restriction on linear independence and demonstrating cancellation of certain Eisenstein series at prime $p$. Furthermore, our investigation generalizes to Eisenstein series of any degree and concludes with an examination of pseudo-Eisenstein series.

This research focuses on the secure control of a mobile robotic arm in a treacherous environment where an autonomous vehicle must navigate through hazards without colliding with them. Since traditional security controllers based on Control Barrier Functions are challenging to apply in this scenario due to the intricate paths of the robot and obstacles, we introduce a novel method using a dynamic layering system. This approach considers the robotic arm's specific arrangements and uses a moving reference frame to simplify the complex geometry, enabling the design of a security controller via the Control Barrier Function framework. Furthermore, we utilize a real-world mobile robotic arm platform to validate our approach via outdoor trials.

This research presents a novel proposal for text summarization using a graphical representation, which combines the strengths of two existing approaches - pointwise rental algorithms and algorithms relying on natural language models - to overcome their individual limitations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through experimental evaluation on summaries produced by the BERT-base-uncased model and a comparative analysis with two established graphical methods. Furthermore, this approach is adaptable to both extractive and full-text summarization frameworks.

Researchers investigated the behavior of an ultracold bosonic gas trapped in an optical lattice under the influence of a nonlinear quantum switch, represented by a combination of laser radiation and Ho\"{e}l-Meyer-Kuizenga light, which imposes an effective phase diffusion process on the system. 
The application of the nonlinear quantum switch led to the observation of a critical point and a condensate fraction peak resulting from a non-stationary condensate fraction maximum at the system's critical temperature.
The experiment was carried out and the dynamics of the system were analyzed through both numerical and experimental approaches.
The findings show that the presence of the nonlinear quantum switch creates a self-organizing critical point with behavior deviating from standard Bose-Einstein critical conditions.

This article aims to comprehend the concept of distinctness for meromorphic mappings from a complete Kähler manifold to a complex projective space, and explore its implications are explored in relation to theorems on the explicit separation of meromorphic mappings.

Polynomial system solving is a critical function with vast potential applications across various fields. However, the methods currently in use have significant drawbacks, such as using an unnecessarily large bassin of attraction for tasks like plotting a complex curve or determining intersections, which leads to unnecessary computations. We introduce an original approach, inspired by the Lissajous-like patterns, to identify non-trivial solutions of a polynomial system, which we complement with a demonstration of its algorithmic viability.

Low-energy direct photons are assessed in copper-copper collisions at a center-of-mass energy per pair of nucleons ($\sqrt{s_{_{NN}}}$) of 200 GeV. Data from the PHENIX experiment, published in 2021, revealed a low-energy photon spectrum that did not conform to predictions made by the pythia and urqmd theoretical models. In an effort to provide a more accurate understanding, the assessment is further refined to incorporate data collected at lower geometric angles relative to the $z$-axis and within a specific range of charged particles' transverse momentum. Nonetheless, the outcome remains inconsistent with both pythia and urqmd predictions, suggesting that a current understanding of the photon extraction process or nuclear interactions is flawed. Alternatively, the presence of a hot, dense medium may give rise to novel physical phenomena.

We investigated the $n$-vertex graph with the minimum $L_2$-norm (or Euclidean norm) for its distinct triple intersections and addressed Turan's tetrahedron problem in this specific context, achieving the following results: For $\alpha$ below a certain threshold, the minimum $L_2$-norm occurs in a certain type of hypergraph with near-optimal triple intersections; in another scenario where $\alpha$ exceeds a certain threshold, the minimum $L_2$-norm occurs in a different, hypergraph with near-optimal triple intersections; Furthermore, we showed that for $n$-vertex graphs with near-optimal tetrahedron-free property and certain properties of their edge and degree spectra, their distinct triple intersections form an isosceles triangle in the $L_2$-norm, where the equality holds when they form an equilateral triangle. These findings improve upon previous findings by Bollobas, and we also showed an equivalence between minimizing $L_2$-norm and a certain face-exclusion problem in convex geometry.

When displaying complex data such as satellite imagery and street maps, combining raster and vector graphics is essential for an enjoyable visual experience. However, the interpolation of raster images during rendering can introduce visual artifacts, particularly noticeable when rendering lines and polygons from vector maps. These artifacts can be mitigated by using spatial anti-aliasing, a graphics rendering technique commonly applied to images, in an effective manner for the representation of line junctions. We present a versatile approach for anti-aliasing line junctions, compatible with various mapping applications, including online and in-car navigation systems, and demonstrate its implementation on a real-world map renderer.

We develop a new RBF quasi-interpolation operator utilizing the B-spline basis, which enables straightforward derivation of the operator's second order partial difference operators without relying on any additional formulations. To achieve this, we design a novel choice of RBF with a distinctive form, allowing it to be linked to a transcendental polynomial. This novel RBF is subsequently linked to the B-spline basis, leading to the development of the new operator. Our work also incorporates a method for approximating high-order derivatives, which serves as confirmation that the proposed operator retains the original smoothness properties of the underlying function.

In a study, researchers examine the northern hemisphere of the galaxy for pulsar wind nebulae, specifically searching for new examples of mature pulsar shells. Using data from the Fermi Large Area Telescope, they conduct a systematic search for 10-sigma sources associated with giant pulsar locations. The analysis confirms the existence of four established pulsar wind nebulae and identifies a novel source, P3SH, linked to PSR J1852+4911. The new source, P3SH, is found to exhibit distinct square-wave-like emission patterns, a feature not seen before in this type of source, and its study provides a maximum age estimate of approximately 171,000 years for the pulsar. The data suggests that P3SH is observed at a relatively young age, specifically between 40,000 to 170,000 years, and its study may offer novel insights into gamma-ray emission produced by pulsar shells.

Transportation systems in many countries are hindered by inclement weather, particularly in locations like UK cities, where roads are frequently closed due to weather conditions. Assessing the severity of weather from vehicle-borne data presents a promising approach for developing an automated system that could aid in transportation system planning and management. In response to the need for standardized weather classification, we have created a new, comprehensive multi-class dataset consisting of 8263 images across five regions, encompassing different types of weather. This dataset is based on the Dataset for the Automatic Recognition of Road Surface Patterns (DARSP) framework, which includes labels for five distinct weather types and recognition of three types of road surface patterns. As transportable vehicles are often equipped with cameras, this methodology enables the collection of weather data throughout a city's entire route system. However, our approach faces a notable challenge: the capture of clear and representative images of adverse weather in a diverse range of locations is complicated due to the inherent variability of weather conditions across different locations. In response to this difficulty, we have developed an image enhancement technique that incorporates knowledge about the relative frequencies of different weather conditions to produce a more reliable dataset for training Convolutional Neural Networks. A comprehensive evaluation of the impact of dataset size, image enhancement, and residual networks on the accuracy of weather classification has been conducted, utilizing the implemented datasets. The results have been compared to the performance of state-of-the-art CNN architectures on the benchmark dataset, SUN_345. The proposed technique yields

The current state of the environment demands immediate global action to avoid severe climate-related disasters, but, as demonstrated by the analysis of the dynamics underlying public awareness about the issue, such widespread cooperation is highly unlikely. Various scientific studies have clearly outlined the gravity of the problem, yet, due to the absence of a central decision-making body, political commitments to address the issue remain fragmented and ineffective, leading to the ongoing deterioration of the Earth's climate system. To achieve a swift and universal response, it is crucial to understand the complex interactions between scientific advice, political institutions, and economic motivations. Through a simplified global climate model incorporating multiple standards for measurement, this research explores the dynamics of public awareness about climate change and the likelihood of achieving a global consensus, providing insights into the mutual influence of scientific warnings, political decision-making processes, and economic interests. The model reveals that the model's stability can be maintained within a safe state only when the coefficients representing the influence of science, politics, and economics are closely balanced. If the system is pushed into an unstable region, it is likely to experience sudden changes, analogous to phase transitions, rendering long-term predictions of public climate awareness and political response impossible. The study suggests that targeting the issue through economic incentives or scientific education alone is insufficient, and, instead, a combination of measures addressing the underlying institutional problems is required.

We introduce an innovative approach to simulate and control soft robotic grippers using advanced mathematical techniques known as the Koopman operator theory. This approach enables the efficient modeling and regulation of flexible robotic arms, even when traditional robotic models are inoperable due to their complex non-linear dynamics. To develop an effective controller, we utilize the underlying spectral properties of the Koopman operator, facilitating the design of a spectral operator that helps achieve desired equilibrium states. To mitigate the requirement for precise system parameter accuracy, we also provide an option for adjusting the controller parameters. The proposed method's performance and flexibility are demonstrated through simulations of a virtual three-fingered robotic hand, as well as with actual physical robots, showcasing its application in soft robotic technology.

Inspired by earlier expositions of gradient descent by Alan Turing and Donald Hebb, we introduce a comprehensive formulation encompassing multiple methods, including the original approaches mentioned above, along with the Levenberg-Marquardt method and others. This formulation is based on the fundamental observation that these methods can be viewed as iterative techniques to solve a data-driven problem, which involves approximating a hidden low-rank matrix. Under this framework, existing methods can be seen as employing varying norms to mitigate noise in estimation problems. Additionally, we highlight the connection to classical Greek mathematician Apollonius' problem and the relationship between matrix norms, which is significant from a mathematical perspective.

A known quasar, J2102+6015, was initially identified through the detection of Lyman absorption in a massive galaxy at the redshift of 4.575, which was found using the XSHOCK dataset's $\sim$1.1 million square degrees of sky coverage. Initially, it was thought that the quasar drove the observed gas outflow due to its high energy emission, but follow-up research revealed that the quasar is not the primary source of the outflow. Instead, the outflow was found to be centered on the quasar and had the characteristics of being radio-powered, with its X-ray spectrum and temporal behavior consistent with those of previously studied radio-powered shocks. The data also showed that the quasar is likely in a continuum of age and strength similar to those of OQ+ 54 and Fall 223, and indicated that J2102+6015 is likely to be the second in a pair of opposing jet-powered shocks, with its counterpart having yet to be identified.

The survival rate for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients varies significantly depending on the stage at which it is detected, ranging from 20% to 30% if caught early but dropping as low as 5% if left undiagnosed. Current imaging methods, such as CT scans, have inherent limitations and risks associated with the exposure of patients to ionizing radiation. As an alternative, researchers have found that machine learning can help improve the accuracy of cancer diagnosis and treatment prediction by utilizing patterns present in medical data. To address these challenges, a new system is introduced that utilizes deep learning to integrate multiple imaging and clinical modalities, aiming to increase accuracy in tumor prognosis and assessment. Education, represented by histopathology images and clinical data, is used to train a model for predicting patient outcomes following lung cancer treatment. By combining CT, PET, and clinical data, the system can determine a patient's likelihood of response to chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and surgery, enabling more informed treatment decisions. Additionally, the model's ability to learn from immunohistochemistry histology images provides valuable information for surgical treatment assessment. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving high accuracy across various datasets, outperforming existing single-modality approaches and surgical treatment assessment models.

A well-structured reference language state is crucial for reinforcement learning methods that utilize pre-built models. However, existing approaches often fail to guarantee semantic coherence between the reference language state and the actual world state. Novel techniques, such as the Offshore Navigation Case Study, have been developed to produce authentic language state descriptions that accurately represent the system's state. These methods hold the potential to enhance the performance of traditional reinforcement learning methods, but require the implementation of a suitable search algorithm to discover feasible plans.

A breakthrough in astrophysics called the $M_{*}$ relation has significant implications for understanding galaxy evolution, and research is ongoing to refine its parameters.  By observing the relationship between a galaxy's stellar mass and the energy released per unit mass (or "mass-energy spectrum"), scientists can determine the rate of star formation across various galaxy types.  Although this information is typically derived from infrared observations of nearby galaxies, a new method is designed to extract this data from highly luminous quasars at greater distances using spectroscopy.  This requires developing a way to "deconvolve" the energy spectrum of these galaxies to determine the rate of star formation.  To improve this process, a machine learning algorithm is being trained using the Coadd catalog of the Dark Energy Survey, and we explore its ability to reconstruct the mass-energy spectrum of galaxies based on this data.

For simple Lie algebras of derivative operators $\frak d$ over a field with two elements, we investigate the properties of vacuum modules in relation to its standard weight modules. It's established that the intersection of all U(\frak h)-vacant modules is comprised of elements with trivial central charges. Furthermore, we establish a one-to-one correspondence between the set of irreducible U(\frak g)^{\frak h}$-modules and the set of irreducible U(\frak h)-modules, where the latter consists of vacuum modules. It remains to be determined how these results extend to Lie algebras of higher orders.

Social media monitoring through sentiment analysis on platforms like Twitter enables
organizations and individuals to track the public's emotions towards them and their rivals.
As a result, analyzing public sentiment has become both crucial and difficult to accomplish.
In this paper, we present our approach to sentiment analysis by investigating various neural
network strategies, finally demonstrating how the Long-Short-Term-Memory model can
effectively classify sentences or tweets as positive, negative, or neutral.

Recent advancements in large language models have shown great potential for
addressing various natural language processing challenges, and their application
in open-domain conversation systems remains an area of ongoing exploration. To
construct such a system, existing solutions typically rely on pre-trained
language models as a starting point and employ transformation and scaling
strategies, keeping the underlying model architecture intact. In this work, a
new approach for building open-domain conversation systems is presented, where
the core language model architecture itself is modified to meet the requirements
of this task. Comprehensive experiments were conducted to evaluate the
performance of this proposed method using multiple open-access datasets and
recent language models, and the results show substantial improvements over
existing solutions.

The presence of gravitational waves in the early universe could lead to a random background of waves with longer wavelengths. The short-term memory of these waves makes them harmless in the long term. However, the long-term memory of gravitational waves, which persists after the short-term waves have dissipated, poses an interesting problem in cosmology, as it may lead to a permanent change in the short-term structure of space-time. The long-term memory of gravitational waves, which varies depending on the direction of propagation, cannot be averaged out, thereby creating a permanent change in space-time that varies by direction. This, in turn, could potentially explain a random background of gravitational waves with longer wavelengths as their short-term counterparts disappear, leaving behind a persistent effect in the form of a permanent change in space-time. Observational evidence for such a effect in the early universe could potentially explain a random background of gravitational waves, which in turn could provide a potential explanation for a part of the observed background radiation.

A hypothetical phase transition within the universe is proposed to explain three phenomena: the origin of matter-antimatter imbalance, the presence of high-frequency gravitational waves, and the existence of supermassive black holes. This phase transition is postulated to have occurred between a SUSY-breaking state and a state of broken SO(10) symmetry, which gives rise to a peV-scale leptogenesis mechanism. Before this transition, it is suggested that a significant degree of symmetry is broken, resulting in a significant number of topological defects, which evolve into supermassive black holes with a mass of approximately $10^16$ grams, thus providing a possible explanation for their observed properties.

A reliable and efficient communication infrastructure is vital for diverse applications such as content distribution, device control, and autonomous driving, which require certain requirements to be fulfilled even in the event of failure. We interconnect a novel form of emergent semantic communication that relies on semantic inference and a signaling game to a neural network that learns patterns in data. We investigate how these components contribute to efficient information transfer by studying an example with a delivery driver who needs to convey information about a package's contents through a failed wireless connection to multiple recipients with distinct capabilities for processing information. We analyze the results of this case study and find that the outcome is not a straightforward binary choice, but rather a complex set of possibilities that depend on various factors, including the driver's strategy and the recipients' abilities to process information, and these results reveal an unexpected connection to the concept of emergentness in complex systems. We discuss several open research questions and propose a promising line of inquiry that involves integrating this form of emergent semantic communication into existing wireless networks.

In the early stages of a document translation project, there is often a high frequency of unfamiliar words, which can hinder effective translation.  To address this issue, term prediction, which suggests potential translations for these unknown words, comes in handy.  Our approach combines a Naive Bayes classifier with latent document information to enhance term prediction quality.  By utilizing information from both relevant documents and infrared datasets, we've developed a hybrid framework that not only accurately classifies unfamiliar words but also provides their probable meanings.  Our results demonstrate significant improvements over existing state-of-the-art term prediction models, with gains of nearly 26% in one case.

Recent sessions-based recommendations techniques have gained significant attention 
due to their potential to utilize users' prior session data for enhanced 
personalization. These sessions-based methods can extract more intricate 
user preferences compared to traditional item-level recommendations, 
particularly when dealing with users who have limited or sparse purchase history.
This paper addresses two critical limitations of existing session-based 
recommendation techniques. Firstly, we focus on addressing the issue of 
recommendation data being biased towards positive items, which can result in 
overemphasizing loud and noisy signals. To this end, we propose a novel 
candidate rank representation for session-based suggestion lists, aiming to 
balance both positive and negative items. Moreover, we introduce a novel rank 
-based loss function for training session-based models, which aims to mimic 
the distribution of suggestion lists in real-world scenarios. Second, we aim 
to explore the potential of using session-based suggestion data for 
generalization across different time phases within a day. We propose a NSBS 
model that extracts both temporal-agnostic and time-phase-specific patterns, 
which can enhance suggestion lists with time-phase aware suggestions. We 
conduct comprehensive experiments on a large retail dataset and demonstrate 
the effectiveness of our proposed methods over state-of-the-art baseline 
techniques. Notably, our models' performance is reflected in up to a 27% 
relative improvement in next-item prediction across various settings.

In recent years, researchers have created highly active soft matter systems in various forms of colloidal solutions, which have significant differences in behavior compared to traditional active matter models. Due to the soft nature of these systems, it's often difficult to generate detailed simulations. This study presents an innovative approach that efficiently simulates complex interactions between active colloidal particles and allows for the adaptation of existing knowledge on active particle movement. By applying a simplified yet accurate method, we analyzed the dynamics and behavior of active particles in activity gradients and discovered novel phenomena, such as altered movement patterns, formations of stable structures, and changes in the particles' diffusion patterns. Depending on the activity level and interparticle forces, the colloidal particles may assemble into various shapes, like clusters, sheets, or whiskers, and their diffusion patterns can be explained by analyzing the system's energy landscape. This work provides a thorough understanding of the dynamics involved and presents findings that match well with actual experimental observations.

This research project delves into the simulation of three-dimensional fluid flow through a fractured porous medium, employing the modified Mimetic Finite Element Method. We model the fractured medium as a porous medium with permeability reduced by a constant factor. By adhering to the continuum approach, we use fluid density and viscosity constants. Our model is validated through comparison with an analytically derived solution for fluid and fracture domain coupling. A two-dimensional mesh quality metric is extended to handle three-dimensional meshes, enabling the simulation of fully permeable fractures. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, as shown in the attached files.

This research introduces an innovative approach to equip a swarm of unmanned aerial vehicles (drones) with the ability to reach locations in a structured environment, undeterred by collisions. Our method utilizes this capacity in the context of biomedical applications, where the architecture of a laboratory can be replicated using aerial robots to carry out experiments in a simulated environment. To implement this approach, we divide it into two components: the registration of point clouds and the planning of drone trajectories. First, we develop a collision-avoidance algorithm based on a centroid-based registration method of the point cloud, which identifies and avoids obstacles by shifting the drone's trajectory to optimize registration. Our approach is then refined to equip each drone with a Collision-Free Field that enables neighboring drones to utilize it for navigation, thus preventing close encounters. To validate our method, we conduct a series of simulations, which demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, along with a drone trial testing its registration capabilities.

This research explores the spectrum and quadratic forms associated with the Seidel matrix of a directed chain graph, demonstrating that all eigenvalues are real, single or paired. We find that the Seidel matrix's positive eigenvalues or energy are influenced by the graph's bipartition and the sizes of its connected components. Specifically, in a chain graph with n components of varying sizes, the Seidel matrix will have up to n eigenvalues with positive real values or pairs, each containing two positive eigenvalues. Additionally, the Seidel matrix's energy or sum of eigenvalues will be less than or equal to n^2. We have also shown that a chain graph of n components with the largest possible sizes of individual components will result in the largest possible number of positive eigenvalues or pairs of positive eigenvalues for the Seidel matrix.

This research investigates a mean-field optimal control issue centered on stochastic differential equations featuring bilinear feedback mechanisms, in the presence of a fractional Brownian motion. Utilizing the variable transformation method, we demonstrate the existence and uniqueness of the necessary and sufficient stochastic Hamiltonian system. Through the establishment of a variational problem, we show that the key stochastic Hamiltonian system is equivalent to solving the original mean-field optimal control issue. Additionally, under the condition that the fractional Brownian motion's Hurst parameter exceeds 0.5, we prove the regularity of the stochastic Hamiltonian system's solution.

For a specific type of Dirac operator defined on a complete, bounded region of n-dimensional Euclidean space, we develop a new approach to determining its finite-band energies. This operator is modified to account for a periodic potential and a zero-order imaginary component. We prove that the finite-band energies it produces converge to a unique limit and that these same energies can be found through the solution of a related model in a bounded, Euclidean space with a different metric. Additionally, we show that the same set of energies can be found by analyzing a related system of periodic Jacobi matrices.

The recent surge in vehicle reliability has been driven by the advancements in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) technologies. Vehicle-to-Roadside (V2R) and Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communications are now capable of supporting safety-critical applications. However, vehicle reliability is hindered by interior and exterior interference. To address this issue, a novel 2-Tier network design is proposed, utilizing Roadside Units and vehicles as relays to boost in-vehicle link quality. By analyzing performance metrics in a real-world scenario, simulations demonstrate that the 2-Tier network can enhance in-vehicule throughput and reliability while reducing end-to-end delay. Furthermore, the results show that the use of vehicles as relays can improve in-vehicule link quality even when the vehicles are moving at moderate speeds.

Wikipedia's vast knowledge base relies heavily on contributions from voluntary editors, both professional and casual. These editors have developed an intricate system of collaboration that seeks to present a unified front of information. However, this endeavor necessitates the removal of redundant, inaccurate, or conflicting information, categorizing it into various types such as "delete" tags. While certain aspects of this process are governed by strict rules, the classification of what constitutes "low quality content" remains somewhat subjective. Despite this, Wikipedia's vetting process of articles relies on identifying and dismissing low quality material, often manually, although this can be done with the aid of text analysis tools. In this research, we aim to investigate the potential of using Wikipedia's rich editorial data to automatically identify patterns in editing behavior associated with low quality content, ultimately propelling the platform towards a more efficient and merit-based rating system for contributing editors.

Current machine learning methods face the challenge of performance decline when new instances need to be classified. Knowledge transfer from experienced experts to less experienced novices or external agents is a promising solution, but it is often restricted by requirements of explicit knowledge sharing. From a decision-based black-box perspective that doesn't require revealing the knowledge, we explore a new approach of zero-shot knowledge transfer. We will demonstrate that, in the absence of any shared information, experienced experts can still pass on valuable insights to less experienced novices or external agents for making better decisions. Furthermore, we will show that these knowledge transfers can be achieved without relying on the actual instances encountered, but rather through generalized decision-based black-box feedback. Such general feedback can be obtained from various sources, like expert judgments or human preferences, and we provide empirical evidence of its effectiveness in improving the decision-making performance of the knowledge recipients.

Researchers have observed the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 K^0_L$ decay mode for the first time, and have also gathered evidence for the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} K^0_L$ decay mode, utilizing a 3.0 $\text{fb}^{-1}$ dataset of $pp$ collisions collected at 7 and 8 TeV center-of-mass energies by the LHCb. The branching fractions for these decays are calculated as follows: The $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^0 \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at (4.3±0.5±0.3±0.3±0.6) ×10^-4, and the $B^0_s\to\bar{D}^{*0} \bar{K}^0$ branching fraction is estimated at (2.8±1.0±0.3±0.4±0.4) ×10^-4, with the given uncertainties stemming from various sources.

We've extended traditional geometric T-duality from torus bundles with flat connections to bundles with twisted connections, adopting a geometric approach that preserves coordinate representation. This new framework applies to a broader range of examples, such as principal SU(3) bundles with singular points. Our results show that T-duals of torus bundles with curvature are torus bundles with curvature, reinterpreting this concept with twisted connections. We've demonstrated that our approach can be generalized to represent any cohomology class in H^3(BG, \Z). Furthermore, our method facilitates the analysis of T-duals with singular points, illustrating the application with a SU(3) bundle as an example.

In recent years, deep learning models have gained significant attention for their potential applications in satellite remote sensing. However, satellite image data collection is a costly and time-consuming process due to the scarcity of satellite resources and scheduling conflicts. This paper introduces a novel, resource-efficient approach that leverages the characteristics of persistent satellite missions to maximize data utilization. We have developed a deep learning method, called the Co-Observation model, which enables the training of models on fewer observation sessions without requiring expert manual data selection. The model's performance depends on the number of available observation sessions and we have demonstrated that our model can effectively learn from the data without expert intervention.

This research introduces a novel method for designing and constructing high-performance Polarization-Aided Cycle (PAC) codes, which are specifically designed to mitigate cycle-based failures in Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing. By integrating polarization metrics from the existing Qubit-based codes, our approach significantly expands the code's potential for fault tolerance while minimizing excess codeword length. We demonstrate the efficacy of our approach by calculating the polarization metrics of several well-established PAC codes, including the polarized versions of the surface code, hexagonal code, and fractal code, and show that they can achieve negligible failure probabilities with moderate code redundancy.

A low-cost, wearable hand-tracking technology is being developed that can handle the complex interactions of human hands with objects in the natural environment. We have created a novel approach to follow the movement of individual hand objects and reconstruct their three-dimensional shapes from time-sensitive cloud point sequences. An efficient algorithm called TIMMO, for "Tracking Instantaneous Hand MOvements," uses color, shape, and temperature data to identify and track the state of each hand object. By assuming a known temperature range for human hands, the technology can accurately detect the state of each hand object relative to the skin and reject background point data, enabling 3D reconstruction of the true position of each hand object through color and shape correspondence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our TIMMO approach with state-of-the-art performance on a public wildlife dataset and real-world wildlife scenarios.

This study employs the transformation semigroup approach to categorize noncrystallographic tail-triangle C-groups of grade 4, with an interlacing number of 2. Our analysis involves constructing a C-grade tail-triangle semigroup of degree 5, and then determining the C-grade subgroups of degrees 3 and 2 within a tail-triangle semigroup of degree 5, having a grade of 4 and interlacing number 2. It's further demonstrated that the C-grade subgroups of degrees 3 and 2 form a combinatorial pair if and only if their corresponding subgroups of degrees 2 and 1 in the horizontal strip have a combinatorial pair. This finding utilises the principles of divisibility in sets of numbers.

A versatile and efficient method is developed for calibrating a depth camera on a robotic system without using specialized equipment or marked points. By utilizing robot joint positions and relying on a learning-based approach, the calibration process becomes straightforward and cost-effective. Additionally, this method leverages the same principles to accurately determine the location of an end-effector on a robotic system, using just a single image, without requiring any marked points, by employing a deep machine learning model. This technique yields excellent results, particularly for scanning tasks and image-based robotic grasping, and is highly adaptable, as demonstrated by its successful implementation in a general-purpose robotic system.

A new framework for analyzing treatment interference in observational studies, the k-nearest-neighbors (KNN) framework, uses a spatial interference model to evaluate the impact of neighboring units on treatment outcomes. To identify the presence of treatment interference in this framework, a testable condition is established for the KNN framework, which does not rely on parametric assumptions. By proving the consistency of the test statistic under different null and alternative hypotheses, the proposed test can effectively determine whether treatment interference exists in a given data set. Empirical analyses of both real and simulated data confirm the good performance of the test in accurately identifying the presence of interference.

Calculations of neutrino emissions from self-destructing dark matter particles within a star have yielded significant insights into the nature of these mysterious particles. Primordial stars, including those of the sun, have been assessed in a previous study, but the current research focuses on the neutrino emissions resulting from dark matter particles annihilating within neutron stars. While an earlier analysis considered the exchange of bosons between these particles, this study examines the effects of a specific type of boson, pseudoscalar $\phi$, on the emissions. The analysis reveals that even at lower dark matter masses than those initially considered, the predicted neutrino counts can still be substantial. The study further estimates that if such a dark matter scenario exists, it may lead to a discovery of the pseudoscalar mediator $\phi$ through its analysis in fast-moving stars, but not through its examination in the sun.

The ongoing UNIONS project, the most comprehensive optical survey to date in the Northern sky, has made its Nickkon $i$-band data of 16713 deg$^2$ available to the community after three years of completion. Following our initial collaboration in photometric redshift analysis, we present the results of combining UNIONS $i$-band data with CFIS redshifts by employing ShapePipe, a newly developed galaxy shape measurement framework. We selected 4900 deg$^2$ of overlapping area between UNIONS and CFIS and utilized \textit{desiLegacy} redshifts as priors to calculate redshifts for the remaining 11710 deg$^2$ of weak-lensing contours. We derived the average redshift of 0.57 for the priors and 0.67 without, and estimated the corresponding shear signal-to-noise ratios of 30 and 18 for the respective areas. We then employed ShapePipe to measure the galaxy ellipticities and calculated two-point shear correlation functions for both areas, which we found to be in agreement with the predicted weak-lensing maps of CFIS. We present the UNIONS $i$-band shaped objects and two-point shear correlation functions, and make available the associated catalogs and figures to the community.

A hypothesis concerning the distribution of non-zero residues has been proposed, which stipulates that for any given trigonometric expression with rational coefficients, the set of points on the torus where this expression exceeds a fixed non-residue value, and the preimage under a Hecke mapping, will have a limit density equal to 1, provided that the magnitude of the Hecke module is sufficiently large. This proposed hypothesis will serve as a cornerstone for a more comprehensive hypothesis concerning the eigenvalue density functions of classical zeta functions and other objects of a similar nature. Notably, a special case of this hypothesis, known as the Chowla conjecture, would yield a significant consequence, confirming that certain number theoretic inequalities naturally approach a limit of absolute value 1. By merging quantities originating from different number theoretic invariants, such as the distribution of non-residue values and zero free zeros, close approximations to integer values can be achieved. Although the full extent of the hypothesis may be unattainable, significant headways can still be made by targeting specific scenarios or combinations of scenarios. A notable instance is when the trigonometric expression can be represented as the sum of square rooted phases, in which case the hypothesis can be verified at a logarithmic scale. This verification relies on the analysis of a system of linear forms with restricted height and depends on the resolution of a particular inequality concerning the size of $n$-tuples of integers. We prove that for k-rational singularities and k-Du Bois singularities, a key property holds: they exhibit symmetrical behavior in relation to nearby variables. Specifically, when a pair (X, D) satisfies certain conditions, with X being a projective variety over k and D a k-Du Bois divisor on X, a significant equivalence emerges: the set of k-rational points on X is equivalent to the set of k-rational points on the pair (X, D). Furthermore, this duality extends to Hodge numbers and mixed Hodge numbers, showing that they remain invariant under the inclusion of variables. This theorem builds upon previous research by many mathematicians, with influences from Goresky-MacPherson, Green-Lazarsfeld, Esnault-Viehweg, Saxce, and others.

We discovered a simple yet effective strategy for manipulating the long-range components of the correlated waves in an experiment using a field-adjustable Hall effect. The sample, made of a thin film with a weakly interacting ferromagnet as the core, showed Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless behavior during the analysis. By adjusting the external field, we were able to isolate the effects of pure spin waves and analyze them in detail. Our research provided strong support for the theory that spin wave interactions are the primary cause of the transition to long-range order in Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phases.

In the absence of an ultra-high-energy particle collider, we investigate a novel theory called the Axion-Sterile Neutrino Shadow Substance (ASeNSS) hypothesis. Within the framework of the ASeNSS, the axion-like particle, with its associated axion-like fields, plays a crucial role in allowing sterile neutrinos to mix with their active counterparts. Using the dark matter decays into X-rays observed in the Virgo Cluster, we evaluate the ASeNSS hypothesis and find that it accommodates the data with a margin of error. Notably, the manner in which the sterile neutrinos are summed over all possible masses in the ASeNSS model tends to soften its constraints when compared to individual mass specifications. Nevertheless, the investigation's findings suggest that the ASeNSS hypothesis is robust enough to be probed through future observations using high-sensitivity technology similar to the one employed by the AXIONSCOPE.

We have developed a series of quantum combinatorial experiments for determining the maximum rank of the stabilizer generators in certain types of quantum error correction codes, known as magic states, given specific resource constraints. The rank of these generators significantly affects the efficiency of the distillation processes used to remove errors from trapped neutral atoms and other types of quantum systems. Our experiments, particularly in constant depth circuits, have led to the discovery of higher upper limits for the rank of the \(W\) and Clifford+Toeplitz stabilizers than previously existing ones, particularly in \(S^{\pm}(\mathbb{C}^4)$, with implications for better error reduction in such systems.

A new approach to quintessence cosmology is developed, incorporating the Tsallis holographic dark energy framework and validating the complexity of the model, thereby providing a more reliable explanation for the accelerated expansion of the Universe. We then analyzed the likelihood of the model's parameters, employing a Gaussian distribution, and verified the stability of its equilibrium points in the phase space. We also probed the complexity of the model by examining its asymptotic behavior, particularly in its interaction with the Universe's scale factor. Furthermore, we investigated the likelihood of the complexity parameter's sign, suggesting a correlation between it and the direct product of the Tsallis and quintessence parameters' values. We have considered two forms of complexity, leading to two distinct equations of state, which together with the Tsallis parameter, constitute a set of three independent equations. We have solved these equations for the quintessence field value, expressing it in terms of the Universe's scale factor. We have utilized two different values of the complexity parameter, resulting in two distinct solutions, which in turn yield different solutions for the Universe's decay parameter. We have plotted the decay parameter against the complexity parameter, providing insight into its evolution. We have calculated the current value of the complexity parameter, restricting its value through integration of the complexity equation, thereby establishing a relationship between the complexity parameter and the Universe's decay parameter.

The Large Sky Area Multiobject Observatory (LAMOST) introduced a new area of research with its time-domain survey, using the LAMOST Exoplanet Survey (LES) to greatly expand the number of stars monitored by narrow fields of view. These fields, known as plates, allow for the observation of variable stars to a magnitude of approximately $18.5$. Our research looked at four LAMOST $K$2 plates and identified 1,713 stars that display at least one change in brightness. Of these stars, 1,236 had never been observed before. Through our analysis, we gathered data on the characteristics of these stars, such as their probability of being two or more star systems, and the stars' overall properties. Our results show the benefits of combining time-domain and spectral data, and also provide the findings in detail.

Unpredictable random number generation is crucial in various fields such as cryptography, biometric simulation, and neural network training, among others. Currently, truly random number generation is primarily achieved through unique properties of PN diodes or advanced technologies like CMOS BEOL processes. We introduce a novel and reliable approach, called TuRaN, which utilizes the inherent structure of standard SRAM cells to generate random numbers with merely a 10% increase in area. We utilize an existing SRAM cell's capacity to produce random data by applying underscaled supply voltage to its memory array. Consequently, the SRAM cell's contents transition into a random state, which can be accessed and converted into binary data. Moreover, the SRAM cell's write cycle allows us to generate a quantity of random bits proportional to the number of times the cell is written. In our experiments, based on 28nm FD-SOI technology, we observed an 86% reduction in energy consumption and a 40% decrease in number of cycles required to generate the same amount of randomness as compared to existing methods.

A fundamental concept in discussions of device-level quantum computing involves utilizing a single electron to switch electronic properties. Although this idea is technically challenging, it becomes more manageable when incorporating a semiconductor material with a confining potential. By designing a system with a confined state that can be efficiently coupled to external devices, the theoretical barriers to implementing single-electron switches are significantly lowered. A detailed examination of a proposed device configuration indicates that it possesses an excellent single-electron conductivity combined with low leakage levels, traits that make it suitable for use in resistive random access memory and potentially quantum gates.

We develop a graphical representation, called Causal Feynman Diagrams, to evaluate complex scattering processes. This method effectively addresses issues that make traditional particle-level diagrams impractical for multi-particle scattering, while also tackling the challenges of modern gauge theories. Our approach is analytical, allowing it to be computed using numerical methods. As an example, we analyze the planar double scattering amplitude in the context of quantum chromodynamics and find that the CFDS method agrees with traditional calculations up to the fourth order. This agreement lays the groundwork for the use of CFDS in quantum chromodynamics calculations beyond fourth order. Additionally, the CFDS method has a runtime advantage over traditional methods, particularly when calculated to the fourth order. This publication introduces the concept of Causal Feynman Diagrams and provides a framework for its future use in particle physics calculations.

One-dimensional quantum walks with two possible states, non-normalized and normalized, evolve differently despite sharing a common starting point.  Normalization helps prevent probabilities from exceeding one, making them applicable to simulate various physical systems.  By comparing the probabilities of finding a walker in a specific state at a given time from both models, researchers can determine if a particular system has entanglement or mixed states.  We derive a direct link between these two models of quantum walks by showing that any normalized state can be expressed as a sum of eigenstates, each multiplied by a corresponding eigenvalue.  We also derive a method to obtain the eigenvalues and corresponding eigenstates of a specific one-dimensional quantum walk.  By applying this link, researchers can compare probabilities of finding a walker in a specific state with time from both models, revealing a precise equality rather than approximation.  Additionally, this link may be applied in other areas of quantum theory for finding similarities and differences between various quantum systems.

This study explores the composition of quark stars composed of strange quarks, made up of $\sigma$, $\omega$, and $\rho$ particles, with a combination of two theoretical models: the Sigma-Omega-Rho model for nuclear matter and two different quantum field theory models for the behavior of quarks. The first, the MIT bag model, treats quarks as isolated particles within a bag, while in the NJL model, quarks interact within a framework that develops a non-linear (gauged) Yang-Mills field. By examining the relationship between the masses of quarks and other particles, we uncover similarities and differences in quark star composition across various assumptions, ultimately analyzing the possible new states of matter that exist at high quark densities.

The optical non-linearity in conventional optomechanical systems is too faint to have significant effects on the transmitted light, even though it's the core component of many optical applications. To overcome this limitation, we've engineered a new q-deformed optomechanical system with an inherently robust and controllable non-linearity. By generating a series of optical auto-resonance transitions, the system produces robust and visible light transmission minima. Not only do these improvements occur simultaneously, but they also attribute to the unique properties of the deformed system. By manipulating the value of 'h', this hybrid system can achieve greater clarity in its light transmission. Furthermore, the theoretical predictions made about the system's parameters, such as the entanglement time, confirm that the optomechanical interaction time can approach the classical boundary of 10 microseconds.

In a scenario where the conservation of R-parity is broken, experiments at the Large Underground Experiment could be challenged by novel decay channels of the double-beta decay daughter nuclei. Specifically, the presence of an R-parity violating interaction may make it difficult to uniquely attribute excess counts observed in 0+ to 0+ transitions, which could occur through both gamma and charged particle activity. To investigate this possibility, we have taken a theoretical approach and considered a specific dual-rotor model as a means to describe the broken R-parity symmetry. Notably, the chosen model predicts the creation of an unpaired quark in the final state of the double-beta decay, which can potentially be detected by tagging algorithms designed to identify hadronic activity. While our analysis may provide valuable insights into the nature of the broken R-parity symmetry, it is also possible that the R-parity is preserved unless experiment results point otherwise.

In this research, we investigate the rotational and orbital phenomena in heterostructures composed of ultrathin metals, semimetals, and semiconductors, paired with a noble gas epitaxial monolayer. By combining theoretical and experimental findings, we reveal a comprehensive view of the rotational and orbital variations, accompanied by a comprehensive classification system.
